leftEvidence.role: Firstborn words before the lodging place
leftEvidence.title: The return journey carries a firstborn warning

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Moses sets out with his wife and sons while the LORD prepares him to confront Pharaoh.
points.right: Israel places lamb’s blood on doorframes while the LORD passes through Egypt and strikes the firstborn.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Israel is called the LORD’s son and firstborn; Pharaoh is warned that refusal will bring the death of his firstborn son.
points.right: Later instructions require circumcision for a male who would share the Passover and give one law to native and foreigner.

payload.posture: The warning to Pharaoh anticipates the later firstborn plague, while Passover also joins protective blood and circumcision requirements.

rightEvidence.role: Blood, firstborn death, and circumcision later in Exodus
rightEvidence.title: Passover later joins blood, firstborn death, and circumcision

payload.tension: The later sequence develops Exodus themes but never calls the lodging-place act an anticipation of Passover.
payload.title: Firstborn warning and later Passover
